summary: The root قنو (qnw) primarily means to keep to or preserve something, especially one's sense of shame or modesty.
lane: 1 قَنِىَ الحَيَآءَ ذ He kept to the sense of shame, or modesty; (S, K;) he preserved it: and i. q. اِسْتَحْيَى : and he kept to [or preserved ] his sense of shame, or modesty. (TA.) -b2- قَنَا غَنَمًا , and , He took for himself, got, or acquired, sheep, or goats [ for a permanent possession ], not for sale. (JK.) -b3- قَنَا , aor. يَقْنُو , inf. n. قُنُوٌّ ; a dial. var. of قَنَأَ , q. v. (TA.)

headwords.def: قَنِىَ الحَيَآءَ He kept to the sense of shame, or modesty; (S, K;) he preserved it: and i. q. اِسْتَحْيَى: and he kept to [or preserved ] his sense of shame, or modesty. (TA.) قَنَا غَنَمًا, and, He took for himself, got, or acquired, sheep, or goats [ for a permanent possession ], not for sale. (JK.) قَنَا, aor. يَقْنُو, inf. n. قُنُوٌّ; a dial. var. of قَنَأَ, q. v. (TA.)

He gained, acquired, or got, for himself, (S, K,) or took for himself, (Mgh,) property, or camels, &c., (S, Mgh,) as a permanent stock, for propagation, (Mgh,) not for merchandise: (S, Mgh:) he made it to be in his possession, not to depart from his hand: (TA:) he acquired it for himself permanently, or for a permanence. See 1.
of the nose: see شَمَمٌ. قنا وُشَّق a name given in Egypt to وُشَّق; also called أُشَّق and أُشَّج. (TA in art. اشق.)

A spear-shaft; (Mgh;) a spear (T, S. K) that is hollow, like a cane; (Az, in TA;) a spear with a head affixed to it. (Msb.) Hence, A subterranean channel, or conduit, for water. (Mgh.) [And A pipe. ] قَنَاةُ الكُوزِ The بُلْبُل [or spout ] of the كوز [or mug ], that pours forth the water. (M, K, in art. بل.) قَنَاةٌ, said to signify بَقَرَةٌ وَحْشِيَّةٌ: see فَنَاةٌ.
and Sheep, or goats, taken for oneself, gotten, or acquired, [ for a permanent possession, ] not for sale. (JK.)
in the prov., خَلَاؤُكَ أَقْنَى لِحَيائِكَ i. q. أَلْزَمُ [as meaning Most preservative: see that prov. in art. خلو, and see قَنِىَ الحَيَآءَ, above]. (S in art. خلو, and Meyd.)
The weaving with one thread white and one thread black. (T, voce نِيرٌ.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
